text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele is expected today to finish talks with parliamentary factions on the new government programme.
- A draft law on the prevention of money laundering is to be submitted to the cabinet this week.
- Latvians spent 201.8 million lats while abroad during 1996 while foreign visitors spent only 108.7 million lats in Latvia.

- Erik Tobiass, an 84-year-old Latvian-born Canadian, accused of genocide during World War II, has again been brought to trial after the cancellation of a previous verdict by the Federal Court of Appeal.

- The government has approved a package of incentives to promote the building of a pulp-mill, expected to cost some one billion dollars. The measures include tax breaks and government support for the plant's construction. South Korean Daewoo and an unnamed U.S. company have shown interest in the project.
